name: domainry-builder-v1
description: Extract an evidence-backed backend dependency PRD from a delivered frontend, then build, evolve, repair, integrate, and verify the matching Domainry source-owned application through one project-visible development TODO. The Skill keeps frontend evidence read-only while settling requirements and domain truth, authors declarative backend/model/*.json metadata, and records evidence-located frontend defects as findings for the frontend owner instead of repairing them. Use for frontend-to-Runtime replacement, new backend projects, existing-project increments, metadata-first backend implementation, Runtime integration, full-stack defect routing, and final verification.
---

# Domainry Builder V1

Use exactly this workflow, in this order:

`requirements → model → apply → verify → done`

There is no parallel workflow, receipt attachment ceremony, continuation route, implementation stage, or hidden stage. The project-visible TODO at `.domainry/development/<session-id>.md` is the only progress record. Set its `Current stage` to one of the five names above. Change it only after the current section is complete, and only to the immediate successor.

Resolve `SKILL_ROOT` from this loaded `SKILL.md`, set `DOMAINRY_CLI="$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-cli"`, and run `"$DOMAINRY_CLI" version --json` before other Builder commands. Never discover another Builder CLI through `PATH` or combine files from different Skill installations.

If the session TODO does not exist, copy [DEVELOPMENT_TODO.template.md](assets/DEVELOPMENT_TODO.template.md) to the exact session path and fill its header. If it exists, resume from its `Current stage`; do not create a second workflow or parallel state file.

## requirements

Read [requirements-and-domain-truth.md](references/requirements-and-domain-truth.md) and [BACKEND_REQUIREMENTS_PRD.template.md](assets/BACKEND_REQUIREMENTS_PRD.template.md). Inspect `frontend/**` only when the project actually contains frontend source, and keep it read-only. Settle domain truth inside this stage: actors and scope, objects and state, actions and transaction/idempotency behavior, calculations and settlement, reports and pagination/export, schedules, notifications, files, and integrations. Platform capabilities may inform implementation later; they do not decide business truth.

Write or update `docs/backend-requirements-prd.md`. Do not advance while an unresolved choice changes an observable business result, authorization decision, amount/unit rule, irreversible external effect, or business-state flow.

## model

Read [backend-model.md](references/backend-model.md) and the [capability index](references/capabilities/README.md), then only the capability references needed by the accepted requirements. Author project-owned `backend/model/*.json` and referenced `backend/reports/*.sql`.

Use the embedded CLI for bounded discovery and validation:

```sh
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" model capabilities --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" model capability --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --key <category>
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" model check --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" model plan --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"
```

## apply

Read [project-mutation.md](references/project-mutation.md). Review the current plan and any destructive/evolution decision. `apply model` is the only normal development release command:

```sh
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" apply model --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" \
  --go-module-path <domain-qualified-module> --product-surfaces <reviewed-surfaces>
```

After materialization, read [ownership-and-extensions.md](references/ownership-and-extensions.md) and implement only the project-owned backend source and tests required by the applied model. Use `apply action-context` or `apply connector-context` for the specific item being implemented. Never create placeholders or edit generated code, manifests, receipts, caches, journals, or Runtime-managed state.

Prepare the delivery-bound implementation packet before editing project source:

```sh
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" apply prepare --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"
```

Check and finalize project source with one direct CLI command:

```sh
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" apply finalize --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"
```

Implement project business-flow tests and every applicable large-scale fixture
script here, run focused tests while iterating, then run the affected backend
test set before advancing. `verify` executes completed tests and captures
evidence; it must not be the first place an entire test suite is authored.

## verify

Read [evidence-levels.md](references/evidence-levels.md), [verification.md](references/verification.md), [production-verification-checklist.md](references/production-verification-checklist.md), and [backend-runtime.md](references/backend-runtime.md). Run structural verification, package the project, start one managed Runtime, and exercise the accepted real-data scenarios. Frontend build/test remains frontend-owned.

Structural verification/package success cannot establish real-data scenario acceptance. Run the highest-risk semantic canary before broader Runtime scenario integration.

```sh
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" verify structure --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" verify package --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" verify runtime start --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --address 127.0.0.1:<port>
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" verify runtime status --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"
```

Treat Runtime identifiers and principal/context values as opaque. Bind acceptance to formal actors, authorization and data scope, durable effects, idempotent replay, denied/error unchanged state, and the current package/database cohort. Stop the managed Runtime when it is no longer needed.

If verification reveals a source defect, return explicitly to the smallest
invalidated apply boundary, repair source and affected tests there, rerun
finalization/structure/package and every stale evidence gate, then re-enter
verify. Never keep the stage labeled verify while first-writing the repaired
business-flow suite. Rebuild a stopped managed SQLite cohort and rotate its
acceptance credentials only with `verify runtime rebuild`; never move or delete
`runtime-process.json`, `runtime.db`, its cohort marker, or acceptance secrets
by hand.

## done

Resolve every in-scope finding, update the TODO to `Current stage: done`, and run the lightweight consistency check:

```sh
python3 "$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-development-todo-check.py" \
  --todo "$PROJECT_ROOT/.domainry/development/$SESSION_ID.md" --expected-stage done
```

Report the delivery identity, changed files, tests, Runtime result, highest evidence level reached, and any explicit non-blocking limitation. Never claim more than the evidence proves.

### Invariants

- One Agent session owns one project TODO through all five stages.
- Requirements and domain truth precede capability mapping.
- `frontend/**` is read-only. Frontend defects are reported to owner `frontend`, not repaired by this Skill.
- Project-owned edits are limited to declarative model/SQL, backend source/tests, requirements PRD, and the current TODO.
- Recoverable command failures stay in the current stage: diagnose, repair the owning source, rerun the direct command, and continue.

# Requirements and domain truth

Use only for the `requirements` TODO section. Produce the accepted backend dependency PRD and freeze domain facts before capability discovery. Do not load model, apply, verification, or acceptance authority at this stage.

## Backend dependency PRD

For a new project or a complete frontend Mock-to-Runtime replacement, create or update `docs/backend-requirements-prd.md` from `assets/BACKEND_REQUIREMENTS_PRD.template.md`. For a light existing-project increment, record an equivalent traceable PRD delta in the current session TODO or update the accepted backend PRD, and reference the unchanged baseline.

A source is structured when its rules live in stable titled/numbered sections citable as `<doc> §N`. If one section states a rule completely, cite it rather than restating it. A reference-mode PRD still carries requirement IDs, classifications, owner/capability mapping, decisions, acceptance criteria, and the matrices, each row citing its source section.

Read frontend evidence, when present, in this order: route/page registry and user journeys; typed application API; Mock adapters/fixtures; state stores and hooks; form/list/detail/report components; permission/menu guards; tests and stories; visible copy. Also read the current explicit requirement and latest accepted product/design documents. Frontend inspection is read-only. Mock or visible behavior proves demand or a current assumption, not a business rule without higher-precedence evidence.

Use this precedence while preserving every conflict:

1. explicit current user decision;
2. latest accepted requirement or design contract;
3. latest implemented frontend behavior;
4. typed API and Mock semantics;
5. frontend tests;
6. legacy/reference implementation.

Classify every item as `confirmed`, `recommended`, `open`, `frontend_only`, or `legacy_reference`. Extract actors, journeys, observable success, objects, fields, relations, queries, commands, states, permissions/scopes, errors/conflicts, calculations, transactions/idempotency, external effects, and presentation-only behavior. Every write operation names authorization, observable validation/error behavior, transaction boundary, idempotency/retry policy, durable result, and acceptance proof.

Build one traceability row per requirement: `demand evidence → requirement ID → Runtime owner/capability → model resource or approved source gap → permission/data scope → acceptance journey`. Account for every backend-bound typed API operation and every route. Matrix cells are phrases; do not repeat table facts in prose.

## Critical ambiguity

Classify every unresolved choice before capability selection. Only `business_blocker` blocks model authoring, and only for the smallest affected slice.

| Decision class | Boundary | Handling | Blocks model? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `business_blocker` | At least two concrete incompatible choices remain, and selecting one changes an explicitly required observable result, authorization allow/deny, amount/unit semantics, irreversible external effect, or business-state flow | Name the choices, affected requirements/model items, and obtain current user or accepted requirement authority | Yes, smallest slice only |
| `contract_discovery` | Runtime-owned formal code, canonical identity/context source, or accepted-fact-to-capability mapping | Defer discovery to the typed client/fixed capability contract; record a Foundation/Runtime gap if absent | No |
| `safe_implementation_decision` | Reversible technical choice preserving the accepted invariant | Defer to the published standard or record one conservative default and evolution path | No |
| `product_follow_up` | Product preference with a fallback that preserves required results | Record assumption, owner, fallback, excluded acceptance scope, and review trigger | No |

Security/privacy omissions default to least privilege, sensitive by default, and no export. An explicit broader-disclosure requirement remains a `business_blocker` until its authorization boundary is confirmed.

Use these nonblocking defaults without inventing product rules:

- Explicit exact decimals, comparisons, or sums do not require absent optional currency/unit/range metadata; block only a comparison/conversion slice where incompatible units change the required result.
- Explicit asynchronous approval may use an independent approval Object while the host remains unchanged until the terminal effect; missing edit/cancel/resubmit preferences are follow-ups.
- An explicitly immutable resource with no required business-role read needs no invented read actor; prove creation through a formal admin/seed path or persistence evidence.
- Weekday/morning intent with no timezone/holiday preference uses deterministic deployment timezone and standard weekday cron; block only explicit incompatible calendar outcomes.

## Domain truth design

Freeze domain facts before asking what Runtime can implement. When requirements contain calculations, historical facts, settlement, correction, or reversal, read [domain-truth-and-settlement.md](domain-truth-and-settlement.md) once and close its ownership, persistence, snapshot, trace, correction, and consumer decisions.

Financial, payroll, points, inventory-cost, and settlement facts remain reproducible after Settings change. If an event locks a result, define the write-side atomic action and immutable snapshot/ledger before its reports.

Before capability discovery, settle these observable Report/export invariants when applicable:

1. List Reports use bounded server pagination, a maximum page size, stable ordering with a unique tie-breaker, an opaque cursor, and explicit `truncated`/`total` semantics.
2. Export uses the same Report, parameters, source hash, authorization, and data Scope; a bounded `0..1000` probe selects synchronous governed CSV or asynchronous paged export.
3. Asynchronous export reauthorizes the current persisted principal before page one and sends requester-only terminal notification.
4. Canonical database compare-and-create reuses accepted/running work or a completed unexpired artifact; `audit_id` is excluded from the fingerprint.

Record the required current-database query-plan evidence and driver (`EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN`, `EXPLAIN FORMAT=JSON`, or `EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON)`) as an acceptance obligation. Capability schemas and G01-G32 technical applicability are deliberately deferred to the model route returned by the machine resume packet.

## 8. Reports, Agent tasks, schedules, notifications, files, and integrations

An asynchronous approval with explicit approved/rejected outcomes may keep pending on an independent approval Object when the host lifecycle defines no pending state; the host remains unchanged until the terminal effect. Unspecified edit/cancel/resubmit behavior is nonblocking, with conservative no-expansion concurrency/idempotency that prevents duplicate effects. For an explicit weekday/morning schedule without timezone or holiday-calendar preference, use the platform/deployment-configured deterministic timezone and standard weekday cron and record the preference as a follow-up. Do not block unless an explicitly required multi-timezone or statutory-holiday distinction changes the demanded outcome.

### Mandatory list Report and export contract

This contract is required whenever a Report returns rows or offers export: bounded server pagination; same-Report bounded threshold probe; fixed routing at 1000 (exhausted `<=1000` synchronous governed CSV, observed row 1001 asynchronous paged job); terminal exact total; canonical fingerprint replay; and completed/failed requester Inbox for the asynchronous branch. Only an unresolved observable business result, permission, amount meaning, or business state blocks affected modeling; Runtime mappings are discovered and reversible technical cells use recorded safe defaults. Every applicable contract still blocks delivery acceptance until proved.

| Requirement ID | Capability | Owner / trigger / schedule | Inputs | Durable output / audit | Agent side-effect mode or Connector/external effect | Identity / allowlist / retry / reconciliation | Permission / scope | Classification | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

Every Report that returns list rows must also close this thin contract before capability discovery. `total` may be exact, estimated, or deliberately omitted, but its meaning must be explicit; `truncated` must distinguish a bounded partial result from an exhausted result.

| Requirement ID / Report key | Result kind | Page contract (`page_size`/`cursor` or platform standard) | Maximum page size + decision source | Stable sort and deterministic cursor tie-breaker | `truncated` semantics | Threshold probe / terminal exact total | `<=1000` synchronous behavior | `>1000` async job and terminal states | Canonical fingerprint/replay identity | Completion/failure notification links (audit/job/artifact) | Download identity / Scope / expiry / audit | Runtime support or owner gap | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

Report prepare performs one bounded threshold probe of the same Report under the same normalized parameters and authorized Scope. Exhaustion at 0..1000 rows returns the governed synchronous CSV with an exact total; observing row 1001 routes to the asynchronous substrate without a separate count/full-result query, and the worker pages to a terminal artifact with the final exact total. Both branches share the canonical fingerprint and atomically replay the same live job/artifact. `audit_id` is excluded from that fingerprint: an equivalent request carrying a new audit must link and close it against the original job/artifact, not return 409 or create a second execution. A separate export-only query, unbounded list, duplicate artifact, or browser-memory pagination is prohibited.

For the asynchronous branch, record how Runtime reconstructs the current persisted project user-role principal inside the frozen workspace, including organization/data-scope and default business-profile facts. Acceptance must distinguish genuine authorization drift (fail closed) from transport-to-worker reconstruction drift (must complete); a static manifest role or synthetic Surface is not valid reauthorization.

Use the four decision classes defined in `requirements-and-domain-truth.md#critical-ambiguity`. A `business_blocker` requires at least two concrete mutually incompatible choices and an exact affected slice where choosing changes an explicitly required observable result, authorization allow/deny result, amount/unit semantics, irreversible external effect, or business-state flow. Each row is a semantic execution contract, not only a case title. Runtime-owned identity/context values are resolved through their formal source and carried unchanged; every scenario uses isolated setup so dependent cases cannot pass from residue. The implementer may add the minimum non-human contrasting identities needed for same-record allow/deny, Scope, and requester-isolation proof; fixture count does not assert product organization or role cardinality.
